# Menew

> Free, open source Mac menu bar app: command palette, clipboard history, window snapping, screenshots, system monitor and on-device AI. No account, no tracking.

Menew 1.92.0 (updated 2026-11-02). Native Swift/SwiftUI app for macOS 14 or later, Apple Silicon and Intel. Free and open source (GPL-3.0). Signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized. Made by Quost.

## One app instead of many

- Instead of Raycast or Alfred: Command palette: apps, actions, math, conversions, quick links and AI (⌃⌥Space).
- Instead of Maccy or Paste: Clipboard history with search, preview, snippets and a paste queue (⌘⇧V).
- Instead of Rectangle or Magnet: Snap windows to halves, corners and thirds with the same ⌃⌥ shortcuts.
- Instead of iStat Menus or Stats: CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network and battery in the menu bar.
- Instead of CleanShot X: Screenshots with arrows, text, blur and pinning on screen (⌃⌥⌘S). Plus screen recording, GIFs and scrolling capture.
- Instead of Amphetamine or Caffeine: Keep the Mac awake for a while, until a time or while an app is open.
- Instead of CleanMyMac: Disk cleaner for caches, logs, big files and duplicates; files go to the Trash. Plus an app uninstaller that removes the leftovers too.
- Instead of Dropover or Yoink: A shelf for dragging files between apps, plus image and PDF tools. Split pages, extract the text (even from scanned PDFs) and password-protect PDFs.

## Features

- System monitor: CPU and GPU with live graphs, memory pressure and swap, disk space and read/write speed, battery health and cycles, and the busiest processes, which you can quit in one click. Optional alerts, and you choose what shows in the menu bar. Turn on your next meeting at the top of the menu, with a Join button for Zoom, Meet or Teams. World clocks show other cities' time, and the command palette converts times like “3pm in Lisbon”. Open today's agenda from the meeting card and copy your free times for the next working days, ready to send. See the battery of your Magic Mouse, keyboard, trackpad and AirPods, with an optional low-battery alert. A 24-hour chart of CPU, memory and battery shows what happened, and which apps used the most battery. See performance and efficiency cores, power draw in watts, SSD health, an alert for runaway apps and a one-click system report. Temperatures in °C for the chip, SSD and battery, plus fan speed. Turn on separate icons and each metric gets its own menu bar icon with its own panel. History goes back 7 and 30 days, and you can build your own alerts, like “CPU above 80% for 10 min”. See your Wi-Fi signal, noise, link speed, channel and band, and every login and background item apps installed. Press “Why is my Mac slow?” for a plain-language diagnosis. Turn on Screen time to see how long you spend in each app, split into focus, neutral and distraction, for today, the week or the month.
- Clipboard history: Text, links, images and files. Instant search, filters, pins and a rich preview. Opens with ⌘⇧V. Pause it for 15 minutes or an hour when you copy something private. Turn on the paste queue to copy several things and paste them one by one with ⌘V, in order. Copy a phone, address, email, tracking code, color or meeting link and Menew offers the right action: call, open in Maps, track, convert or join. Search finds text inside copied screenshots and images too, read on your Mac. Share any item with the macOS share menu (AirDrop, Messages, Mail). Search by meaning too: “the hotel link from yesterday”, “that Xcode error”, “images from today”.
- Quick actions: Brightness for every screen, external monitors included. Mute the mic or the sound, hide the Dock, dark mode, keep awake with a timer, hidden files and desktop icons. Plus color picker, screenshots you can annotate, blur and pin on screen (⌃⌥⌘S), eject disks and more. Keep Awake also works until a set time or while an app is open. Switch the sound output and microphone (AirPods, headphones, speakers) in one click, and turn on presentation mode before sharing your screen. Record the screen as video or GIF, or take a scrolling capture of a whole page. The notch comes alive too: a meeting about to start with a Join button, recording time, timers and a muted mic show up next to the camera. In clipboard images and pinned screenshots, select text or click links and phone numbers (Live Text). And remove the background from a photo in one click. Take a photo or scan a document with your iPhone and it lands right on the clipboard, on the shelf, or as text.
- Free up space: Clear caches, logs and developer junk in seconds. A deep scan finds old downloads, large files and duplicate files for you to review. Removed files go to the Trash.
- Internet: Live download and upload, local and public IP, and a real speed test powered by macOS itself. See which apps are using the network right now.
- Notes, snippets & devices: Notes with #tags and Markdown checklists, protected notes that open with Touch ID, password notes with hidden fields you copy in one click, and reusable snippets in ⌘⇧V. Give a snippet an abbreviation like “;sig” and typing it anywhere turns it into the text. Snippets can fill in the date, ask for a name before pasting and place the cursor where you want.

## More features

- Monitor brightness — a slider for every screen, including third-party monitors over DDC/CI. Monitors behind an adapter that blocks DDC are dimmed by software instead.
- Mute your mic — from any app with ⌃⌥⌘M, great for meetings. And rewrite any selected text with ⌃⌥⌘R: fix, clearer, more formal, shorter.
- Window manager — snap windows to halves, corners and thirds with ⌃⌥ shortcuts or a grid, and send them to the other display. Or just drag a window to an edge or corner.
- Command palette — press ⌃⌥Space to find any app, action, window layout, snippet or note. Type “brightness 60” or “awake 2h”. Do math and conversions too: “20% of 340”, “5 km to mi”. And it transforms the text you copied: UPPERCASE, camelCase, format JSON, Base64, count words. For developers: see which ports are in use and stop the server, generate a UUID, turn a Unix timestamp into a date and decode a JWT. Menew's actions also show up in Siri, the Shortcuts app and Spotlight, ready to use. With Apple Intelligence it also summarizes, rewrites, fixes and translates the text you copied, using only the model on your Mac. Quick links open sites straight from it: “g coffee”, “gh menew”, “maps paulista”, or your own like “jira ABC-123”. Ask it anything starting with “ai” and the answer appears in a small window, written on your Mac. In notes, AI summarizes or pulls out the to-dos as a checklist. Read a QR code from the screen, or show a QR of copied text, a link or your Wi-Fi for your phone. Type “remind pay the bill tomorrow at 9” to create a reminder in the Reminders app. Find emoji (“emoji rocket” or “:fire”) and symbols like →, °, € or ✓ and paste them anywhere. Translate the copied text offline with Apple's translator, even without Apple Intelligence. Set a timer (“timer 10m tea”) or an alarm (“alarm 7:30”) with a countdown in the menu bar. Drop your own scripts (shell, Python, Node, AppleScript) in the scripts folder and each one becomes a command, Raycast-style. Or just say what you want: “do dark mode, keep awake and open Safari” and the Mac’s own AI lines up the steps for you to confirm.
- Work profiles — save your open apps and window layout, then bring it all back with one click: apps open, windows go back in place, mic and Keep Awake set.
- Quick shelf — shake files while dragging and a shelf appears. Drop files, links and text there, then drag them all out together. Originals never move. Photos on the shelf can be converted to JPG, PNG or HEIC, shrunk in bulk or stripped of location and metadata, without touching the originals. PDFs too: combine, compress, rotate or turn pages into images. Drop a recording or video and get the transcript as a note, offline.
- Automations — at 9 AM turn on your work profile, mute the mic when Zoom opens, dim the screen when you unplug, quit everything when a focus session starts, run one of your Shortcuts a minute before a meeting or when the Mac wakes. Simple triggers, no scripts.
- Copy text from screen — press ⌃⌥⌘T, select any area (a video, a PDF, an error message) and its text goes to the clipboard. Works on copied images too. Runs entirely on your Mac. Or ask about it: “explain this error”, “translate this”, “what should I do?”, answered by your Mac’s own AI.
- Focus timer — start 25 minutes (or any time: type “focus 50” in the palette) and the countdown shows in the menu bar. It can mute the mic, keep the Mac awake and pause the clipboard, then puts it all back and gives you a 5-minute break.
- App control — quit all apps, quit everything but the one you're using, hide the rest or force quit a frozen app. A work profile can close everything else and open only what you need, and an automation can quit all apps when the battery hits 5%.
- Live notch: An upcoming meeting with a Join button, recording, timers and a muted mic show next to the camera. Gone when there is nothing to show. Rest the pointer on it for your next meeting, the timer and shortcuts, or drop files on it to keep them on the shelf.
- Widgets: System, meetings, timers and screen time on your desktop or in Notification Center. Click to open Menew.
- Siri, Shortcuts and Spotlight: Ask Siri how your Mac is doing, chain 27 actions in the Shortcuts app and find your notes in Spotlight. And Focus filters: with your Work Focus on, Menew pauses the clipboard or quiets the notch on its own.
- Live captions: Your Mac’s audio or the microphone turns into captions in a small window, translated as you go. Great for calls and videos in another language.
- Battery care: Alerts at 80% on the charger and when the battery gets hot, and shows how much health it lost over the months.
- Menew window and Memory: Press ⌃⌥⌘K to save what’s on screen: Menew reads the text, notes the app and link, and AI adds a title and tags. Then just ask: “which was that charts library?”, and AI answers with the sources. And in the graph, see how the topics connect.
- Recordings with minutes: Press ⌃⌥⌘G and talk or take your call: your Mac transcribes it, tells you apart from others, and AI writes the minutes with tasks and tags.
- History up to 30 days: CPU, memory and battery over 24 hours, 7 or 30 days, and the apps that used the most.
- Sensors and cores: Chip, SSD and battery temperatures, fan speed and every performance and efficiency core.
- Network and Wi-Fi: Live speed, the apps using the network and your Wi-Fi signal, noise, channel and band.
- App uninstaller: Removes an app with the preferences, caches and data it left behind. Everything goes to the Trash.
- Login and background items: See which agents and services apps installed to start with your Mac or run hidden.
- Screen time: Time per app for the day, week or month, split into focus and distraction. Off until you turn it on. Now by kind of app (development, communication, entertainment…), and you decide how each one counts.

## FAQ

### Is Menew really free?

Yes. Menew is free and open source under the GPL-3.0 license: no ads, no subscription, no paid tier. If it helps you, you can buy the author a coffee, but nothing in the app asks for it.

### Does Menew collect my data?

No. There is no telemetry, no analytics and no account. Clipboard history and notes stay on your Mac. The only network calls are the update check, your public IP, a speed test you start and a currency rate you ask for. AI features use Apple's on-device model only.

### Which Macs does it run on?

macOS 14 Sonoma or later, on Apple Silicon and Intel. The AI features need macOS 26 or later with Apple Intelligence turned on.

### How do I install it?

Download the DMG and drag Menew to Applications, or use Homebrew: brew install --cask menew after adding the quost/menew tap. Updates arrive automatically.

### Is it safe to install?

Menew is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple, and all of its source code is public on GitHub.

### Can I turn off the parts I don't use?

Yes. In Settings → Modules you can turn off Clipboard, Actions or Notes, and they disappear completely. With Clipboard off, Menew doesn't even read it.

### Is Menew a free alternative to Raycast, Maccy, Rectangle and iStat Menus?

Yes. Menew covers the essentials of each in one app: a command palette and clipboard history like Raycast and Maccy, window snapping with the same shortcuts as Rectangle, and system monitoring with sensors and history like iStat Menus. Those apps still go deeper in their own niche, for example Raycast's extension store.

### Does the AI need the internet or an account?

No. Menew only uses Apple's on-device model (Apple Intelligence), so text, screenshots and questions never leave your Mac. There is no API key, no account and no extra cost.

### What if my Mac doesn't have Apple Intelligence?

Everything else works the same. The AI features tell you how to turn Apple Intelligence on instead of failing, the slow-Mac diagnosis still lists what is wrong, and the smart clipboard search works without it.

### How do I uninstall Menew?

Quit Menew from its menu and drag it from Applications to the Trash, or run brew uninstall --cask menew. Your history and notes live in ~/Library/Application Support/Menew, which you can delete too.

### Does Menew slow down my Mac or drain the battery?

Menew is a native Swift app, not a web wrapper, and the download is about 8 MB. It reads system stats every 2 seconds, takes heavier readings only while you look at them, and features like screen time stay off until you turn them on.

### Which languages does Menew speak?

English, Portuguese, German, Spanish and Simplified Chinese. It follows your macOS language, and you can pick another one in Settings.

## Install

- Download: https://github.com/Quost/menew/releases/latest/download/Menew.dmg
- Homebrew: `brew tap quost/menew https://github.com/Quost/menew && brew install --cask menew`
